title: Deposit Operations Standing Instruction: Dormancy and Reactivation of a Personal Checking Account
content:
**Customer-initiated activity.** Customer-initiated activity on a Personal Checking account means a deposit or debit the owner initiates through a branch, a cash machine, a debit card, a paid check, a mobile deposit, an online transfer, a person-to-person payment, a wire or a direct debit the owner authorized. Interest credits, charges, refunds of charges, direct deposits and other incoming automated credits are not customer-initiated. The account record carries the posted date of the latest customer-initiated activity.

**When an account becomes dormant.** An active account becomes dormant once the tier's number of calendar months has passed after the last customer-initiated activity. Count calendar months from that date; the account is due for dormancy when the frozen date is on or after that date plus the tier's months, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist.

**While dormant.** The tier's dormant account charge is assessed at each statement cycle close, reduced so that it never takes the ledger balance below zero, and not written at all where the balance is already zero or below. Dormancy never stops interest crediting or the posting of incoming credits.

**Reactivation.** A dormant account is reactivated only when the owner's identity has been verified in the current contact and the owner initiates a transaction; the reactivation date becomes the new date of last customer-initiated activity. The identity of the owner must be verified before a dormant account is reactivated, and the verification record is the authority for that.

**Worked illustration of the charge floor (hypothetical).** A dormant account carrying 3.20 on a tier whose dormant charge is 5.00 is charged 3.20, leaving zero, because the charge never takes the balance below zero. An account already at zero is charged nothing.
